programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S]

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Joining Alan this time are film Calendar Girl Celia Imrie to talk about her latest novel and critically-acclaimed novelist Sebastian Faulks - we also meet rare-breed geese and Alan takes up the ancient art of chair caning.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue is joined in her kitchen by designer and TV presenter Patrick Grant, who cooks a delicious slow-cooked fenugreek lamb dish and tells Prue how he inherited his love of cooking from his dad along with an old spice rack which he still uses at home - no-knead focaccia is also on the menu for Prue, who explains that it takes a bit of patience but is well worth the wait. Flavoured with rosemary, salt and olives, Prue declares that this is a dish you should definitely find the time to make - meanwhile, John builds a dovecote for the garden which proves to be a bigger and bolder project than any that have come before, and Prue's food hero is a cake-maker who made a royal wedding cake. John then joins Prue in the kitchen for afternoon scones - including an unusual option of butternut squash scones served with whipped goats' cheese and red peppers - and Prue has a hack for the best way to cut a celebration cake.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S]

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Dermot brings his journey to a close on the surf-battered shores of Strandhill, paddling out with Rebelle Surf into the cold Atlantic to understand why these waves draw people from across the world. He meets a couple who've eaten their way around the globe and landed here, bringing the bold, smoky flavours of the Basque country to the beach in Strandhill. Together they cook turbot over fire, a dish where Ireland and Spain meet to make something delicious. Then it's Dermot's turn. Joined by a host of faces he's met along the way, he takes everything he's seen and eaten along the series. He cooks a proper feast: fresh seafood, a deep, warming stew, and a fruit dessert that carries the sweetness of the whole journey. From the Causeway Coastal Route to the Wild Atlantic Way, it's a meal that tells the full story of the road behind him.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Causton is buzzing at the opening of a new brewery on the site of a famously cursed Abbey. However, excitement turns to fear when a man is found boiled to death in one of the vats. DCI Barnaby and DS Winter are puzzled; could this really be about beer?

programme.title: Thunderball
programme.desc: The fourth entry in the James Bond film series. Led by one-eyed evil mastermind Emilio Largo, the terrorist group SPECTRE hijacks two warheads from a NATO plane and threatens widespread nuclear destruction to extort 100 million pounds. James Bond is sent to recover the warheads from the heart of Largo's lair in the Bahamas - while facing underwater attacks from sharks and men alike, he must also convince the enchanting Domino, who serves as Largo's mistress, to become a key ally in his mission.

Flavoured with rosemary, salt and olives, Prue declares that this is a dish you should definitely find the time to make - meanwhile, John builds a dovecote for the garden which proves to be a bigger and bolder project than any that have come before, and Prue's food hero is a cake-maker who made a royal wedding cake. John then joins Prue in the kitchen for afternoon scones - including an unusual option of butternut squash scones served with whipped goats' cheese and red peppers - and Prue has a hack for the best way to cut a celebration cake.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Dermot brings his journey to a close on the surf-battered shores of Strandhill, paddling out with Rebelle Surf into the cold Atlantic to understand why these waves draw people from across the world. He meets a couple who've eaten their way around the globe and landed here, bringing the bold, smoky flavours of the Basque country to the beach in Strandhill. Together they cook turbot over fire, a dish where Ireland and Spain meet to make something delicious. Then it's Dermot's turn. Joined by a host of faces he's met along the way, he takes everything he's seen and eaten along the series. He cooks a proper feast: fresh seafood, a deep, warming stew, and a fruit dessert that carries the sweetness of the whole journey. From the Causeway Coastal Route to the Wild Atlantic Way, it's a meal that tells the full story of the road behind him.

programme.title: DNA Journey
programme.desc: Comedians and best mates Rob Beckett and Romesh Ranganathan embark on a road trip to find out about their family history using a mix of DNA and genealogy and meet family they never knew existed - while there are plenty of belly laughs along the way, there's also some surprising and moving emotion from TV's top funny men. Romesh really wants to connect to his Sri Lankan heritage after growing up in Crawley, while South Londoner Rob is simply hoping that his family aren't all 'wrong'uns' - however, things don't start well for Rob as he finds out his family in the past are well acquainted with the local prison before finding out that his hero ancestor turned the family's fortunes around with some Beckett determination and grit. Meanwhile, Romesh finds out to his joy and horror that he comes from a dynasty of Ayurvedic doctors in Sri Lanka along his paternal line - while expressing pride at what his family achieved from humble beginnings, he worries about his mother Shanthi finding out...

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James arrives in the misty gardens of Claude Monet's house in Giverny and walks across its iconic Japanese bridge to gaze at the water lilies made famous by the artist - Monet loved his food and had quite a brood to feed, with he and his second wife having had eight children between them. Thinking of this hungry horde, James sets up his mobile kitchen nearby to cook a delicious dish of crab - James's self-confessed idea of heaven - and dulse. There is a peek inside Monet's kitchen as James hears how he collected recipes from the various restaurants at which he dined - meanwhile, Eric Guerin serves pike - one of Monet's favourite fish - at his restaurant Le Jardin des Plumes just down the road. In a nearby orchard on the day of their annual harvest, James prepares an autumnal treat of apple doughnuts - when back home, he then cooks a Normandy tart and a very original omelette.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James arrives in the misty gardens of Claude Monet's house in Giverny and walks across its iconic Japanese bridge to gaze at the water lilies made famous by the artist - Monet loved his food and had quite a brood to feed, with he and his second wife having had eight children between them. Thinking of this hungry horde, James sets up his mobile kitchen nearby to cook a delicious dish of crab - James's self-confessed idea of heaven - and dulse. There is a peek inside Monet's kitchen as James hears how he collected recipes from the various restaurants at which he dined - meanwhile, Eric Guerin serves pike - one of Monet's favourite fish - at his restaurant Le Jardin des Plumes just down the road. In a nearby orchard on the day of their annual harvest, James prepares an autumnal treat of apple doughnuts - when back home, he then cooks a Normandy tart and a very original omelette.

John then joins Prue in the kitchen for afternoon scones - including an unusual option of butternut squash scones served with whipped goats' cheese and red peppers - and Prue has a hack for the best way to cut a celebration cake.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Dermot brings his journey to a close on the surf-battered shores of Strandhill, paddling out with Rebelle Surf into the cold Atlantic to understand why these waves draw people from across the world. He meets a couple who've eaten their way around the globe and landed here, bringing the bold, smoky flavours of the Basque country to the beach in Strandhill. Together they cook turbot over fire, a dish where Ireland and Spain meet to make something delicious. Then it's Dermot's turn. Joined by a host of faces he's met along the way, he takes everything he's seen and eaten along the series. He cooks a proper feast: fresh seafood, a deep, warming stew, and a fruit dessert that carries the sweetness of the whole journey. From the Causeway Coastal Route to the Wild Atlantic Way, it's a meal that tells the full story of the road behind him.

programme.title: The Veil
programme.desc: Summer Heat. 1958. Stars Boris Karloff, Harry Bartell & Paul Bryar. A man watches neighbours across a courtyard and believes he has witnessed a murder, no one will accept his disturbing claims. [S]

programme.title: The Greed of William Hart
programme.desc: 1948. Horror. Directed by Oswald Mitchell and screenplay by John Gilling. Set in Edinburgh in the 1800s and starring Tod Slaughter as William Hart the infamous body broker. [S]

programme.title: Cinebox Memories
programme.desc: The electrifying Screamin' Jay Hawkins performs the 1957 song Frenzy.

programme.title: Green Hornet Strikes Again
programme.desc: The Flaming Inferno. 1941. Starring: Warren Hull. Arson and an insurance scam, lead the Green Hornet to confront shady warehouse owner Crawford about the racketeers' latest criminal endeavour. [S]

programme.title: The Adventures of Sir Lancelot
programme.desc: Knight's Choice. 1957. Stars William Russell, Cyril Smith & Ronald Leigh-Hunt. A Round Table knight has died which means a tournament begins to replace him. [S]

programme.title: Honey West
programme.desc: 1965. King Of The Mountain. Classic crime series produced by Aaron Spelling and starring Anne Francis. Honey goes undercover as a nurse.

programme.title: Enter the Lone Ranger
programme.desc: 1949. Western. Directed by Geroge B. Seitz Jr. Stars Clayton Moore & Jay Silverheels. The sole surviving Texas Ranger of a murderous ambush becomes the great masked hero who fights for justice. [S]

programme.title: Strange Voyage
programme.desc: 1946. Adventure. Director: Irving Allen. Stars Eddie Albert & Forrest Taylor. An adventurer rents a sailing ship to hunt for a treasure and winds up battling bad weather, rough seas and the crew. [S]

programme.title: The Jackals
programme.desc: 1967. Western. Directed by Robert D. Webb. Stars Vincent Price, Diana Ivarson & Robert Gunner. In South Africa, a wily old gold miner and his granddaughter are besieged by a group of bank robbers. [S]

programme.title: The Beverly Hillbillies
programme.desc: Jed Foils a Home Wrecker. 1964. Stars Buddy Ebsen, Irene Ryan & Donna Douglas. Mrs Drysdale hires a demolition man. The Clampett's think a ''home wrecker'' is breaking up the Drysdale's marriage. [S]

programme.title: Batman
programme.desc: Surf's Up! Joker's Under! 1967. Stars Adam West, Burt Ward & Yvonne Craig. The Joker plans to become king of surfing, when all other contestants drop out of the surfing match, Batman steps up. [S]

programme.title: The Battle of the Rails
programme.desc: 1946. War. Directed by René Clément. Stars Marcel Barnault & Jean Clarieux. The story of the brave railroad workers in the French Resistance and their efforts to sabotage the Germans during WWII. [S]

programme.title: A Tale Of Two Cities
programme.desc: 1958. Drama. Directed by Ralph Thomas. Stars Dirk Bogarde, Dorothy Tutin, Cecil Parker & Stephen Murray. During the French Revolution, Lucie Manette falls in love with a duplicitous Englishman. [S]

programme.title: For the Love of Ada
programme.desc: Sunday Tea. 1970. Stars Wilfred Pickles, Irene Handl & Jack Smethurst. Ada invites Walter for Sunday tea with the family, but things change when Mrs Bingley answers the door. (S1, E02) [S]

programme.title: The Man from U.N.C.L.E
programme.desc: The Gazebo in the Maze Affair. 1965. Stars Robert Vaughn, David McCallum & Leo G. Carroll. G. Emory Partridge is seeking revenge on Solo and U.N.C.L.E for foiling a plot seven years earlier. [S]

programme.title: The Footage Detectives
programme.desc: This week's blast from the past incudes a reel from 1953's Coronation Fair, a sneak into the secret Cabaret Club & we go offshore to remember Radio North Sea International. [S]

programme.title: The Directors
programme.desc: Howard Hawks early years began with Cary Grant in Bringing up Baby and His Girl Friday then later with The Big Sleep and Rio Bravo with John Wayne. [S]

programme.title: That's My Boy
programme.desc: Ring If You Need Me. 1984. Stars Mollie Sugden, Christopher Blake & Jennifer Lonsdale. Ida waits on bedridden Mrs. Price hand and foot, but goodwill only stretches so far. [S]

programme.title: The Mosquito Coast
programme.desc: 1986. Director: Peter Weir. Stars Harrison Ford, Helen Mirren & River Phoenix. An inventor spurns his city life and moves his family into the jungles of Central America to make a utopia. [S]

programme.title: Remember My Name
programme.desc: 1978. Drama. Director: Alan Rudolph. Stars: Geraldine Chaplin, Anthony Perkins & Moses Gunn. Just released from prison, a woman arrives in town to start a new life. Soon starting trouble. [S]

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James arrives in the misty gardens of Claude Monet's house in Giverny and walks across its iconic Japanese bridge to gaze at the water lilies made famous by the artist - Monet loved his food and had quite a brood to feed, with he and his second wife having had eight children between them. Thinking of this hungry horde, James sets up his mobile kitchen nearby to cook a delicious dish of crab - James's self-confessed idea of heaven - and dulse. There is a peek inside Monet's kitchen as James hears how he collected recipes from the various restaurants at which he dined - meanwhile, Eric Guerin serves pike - one of Monet's favourite fish - at his restaurant Le Jardin des Plumes just down the road. In a nearby orchard on the day of their annual harvest, James prepares an autumnal treat of apple doughnuts - when back home, he then cooks a Normandy tart and a very original omelette.

Flavoured with rosemary, salt and olives, Prue declares that this is a dish you should definitely find the time to make - meanwhile, John builds a dovecote for the garden which proves to be a bigger and bolder project than any that have come before, and Prue's food hero is a cake-maker who made a royal wedding cake. programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Dermot brings his journey to a close on the surf-battered shores of Strandhill, paddling out with Rebelle Surf into the cold Atlantic to understand why these waves draw people from across the world. He meets a couple who've eaten their way around the globe and landed here, bringing the bold, smoky flavours of the Basque country to the beach in Strandhill. Together they cook turbot over fire, a dish where Ireland and Spain meet to make something delicious. Then it's Dermot's turn. Joined by a host of faces he's met along the way, he takes everything he's seen and eaten along the series. He cooks a proper feast: fresh seafood, a deep, warming stew, and a fruit dessert that carries the sweetness of the whole journey. From the Causeway Coastal Route to the Wild Atlantic Way, it's a meal that tells the full story of the road behind him.

Romesh really wants to connect to his Sri Lankan heritage after growing up in Crawley, while South Londoner Rob is simply hoping that his family aren't all 'wrong'uns' - however, things don't start well for Rob as he finds out his family in the past are well acquainted with the local prison before finding out that his hero ancestor turned the family's fortunes around with some Beckett determination and grit. Meanwhile, Romesh finds out to his joy and horror that he comes from a dynasty of Ayurvedic doctors in Sri Lanka along his paternal line - while expressing pride at what his family achieved from humble beginnings, he worries about his mother Shanthi finding out...

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James arrives in the misty gardens of Claude Monet's house in Giverny and walks across its iconic Japanese bridge to gaze at the water lilies made famous by the artist - Monet loved his food and had quite a brood to feed, with he and his second wife having had eight children between them. Thinking of this hungry horde, James sets up his mobile kitchen nearby to cook a delicious dish of crab - James's self-confessed idea of heaven - and dulse. There is a peek inside Monet's kitchen as James hears how he collected recipes from the various restaurants at which he dined - meanwhile, Eric Guerin serves pike - one of Monet's favourite fish - at his restaurant Le Jardin des Plumes just down the road. In a nearby orchard on the day of their annual harvest, James prepares an autumnal treat of apple doughnuts - when back home, he then cooks a Normandy tart and a very original omelette.
